turns.doctor_question: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response:
Hi, Dr. Smith. I'm Santiago. I'm here because... well, I've been having this issue with eating lately. 

What really worries me is that once I start picking at food late at night, I just can't seem to stop. I'll tell myself, "That's enough, Santiago," but my hand just keeps going back for more. It's almost like I don't get to make the decision anymore.

symptom_reasoning.S050: The patient reports being unable to stop eating late at night and feeling like he no longer gets to make the decision, indicating a sense of loss of control over eating.

turns.doctor_question: After one of these late-night eating episodes, do you ever try to 'make up for it'—for example by making yourself vomit, using laxatives, fasting, or exercising intensely?
turns.patient_response: No, I don't do any of that. I don't make myself throw up or take anything like laxatives. And I definitely don't exercise like crazy or stop eating the next day. I usually just... well, I just feel pretty bad about it the next morning, but I don't try to make up for it like that.

symptom_reasoning.S047: The patient explicitly denies engaging in non-purging compensatory behaviors, stating they definitely do not exercise excessively or stop eating the next day.
symptom_reasoning.S048: The patient explicitly denies purging behaviors, stating they do not make themselves vomit or take laxatives.

turns.doctor_question: How often would you say these episodes of feeling out of control with eating happen, and how long have you been experiencing this pattern?
turns.patient_response: Well, for the past several months, I'd say it's been happening most weeks... at least once a week, anyway. It usually happens on a night when there are plenty of leftovers around the kitchen, and everyone else has already gone to bed so I'm just up by myself.

turns.doctor_question: During these late-night eating episodes, would you say you're eating an amount of food that's clearly larger than what most people would eat in that same amount of time?
turns.patient_response: Yeah, definitely. On some nights after work, I can go through... well, several tamales, a really big bowl of pozole, some tortillas, and just whatever rice or beans are left sitting out. I do all of this just standing there in the kitchen, almost like I'm just... cleaning up the leftovers, you know? But it's a lot of food. It's definitely more than what a normal person would eat in that short amount of time.

symptom_reasoning.S049: The patient explicitly confirms eating an unusually large amount of food within a short period of time, detailing multiple portions and agreeing that it is definitely more than what a normal person would eat.

turns.doctor_question: Do you find yourself eating alone during these episodes specifically because you feel embarrassed or self-conscious about how much you're eating?
turns.patient_response: Yeah, that's exactly it. I just... I don't like anyone seeing how much I put away. It's embarrassing. So I wait until my aunt and the rest of the house are asleep, and I just try to keep it quiet in the kitchen so nobody comes out and catches me.

symptom_reasoning.S054: The patient explicitly confirms eating alone late at night because they feel embarrassed about how much food they consume and want to avoid being seen.
